absent: Locking and concurrency rules for topology and machine check state are not shown in these fragments.
Numeric values of domain tables, domain limits, invalid type codes, and global topology shifts are not shown.
MSR numbers, bit layouts, and control register semantics beyond the named behaviors are not shown.
Behavior of CPUID helpers, MSR helpers, per CPU helpers, logging helpers, and APIC helpers is not shown.
Vendor quirk contents, threshold restart mechanics, timer setup, pool allocation, and late error dispatch are not shown.
Early versus late topology population and symmetric multiprocessing bringup ordering outside these fragments are not shown.

findings.text: Provides a query that converts an APIC identifier to a dense logical index at a requested topology level. It derives a level identifier, rejects out of range and unpopulated values with distinct negative errors, and otherwise counts populated predecessors.

Provides per CPU machine check initialization used during CPU identification. It honors a global disable flag and then moves through legacy handling, availability gating, capability capture, record pool setup, timer plus generic plus vendor setup, bank preparation, and control register enablement.

Provides AMD specific machine check feature setup for the current processor. It applies quirks, marks threshold support, enables scalable MCA interrupt vectors, and walks banks and blocks to configure thresholding where hardware reports usable entries.

Provide legacy machine check enablement for early families. The Intel Pentium path is gated by a global enable and a feature flag and performs diagnostic reads before enabling, while the Winchip path adjusts feature control state and then enables.
Provides access to the firmware derived corrected error threshold limit by returning a stored global value in the threshold handling build.
Early boot entry that populates the vendor driver table from linker delimited entries bounded by a vendor count, optionally logs supported processors, and identifies the boot processor.

Per CPU identification entry that establishes defaults, runs generic discovery, parses topology, invokes vendor hooks, normalizes capabilities, assigns model identity, initializes protection features, merges symmetric multiprocessing capability sets, and starts health and NUMA association.

Topology enumeration views a CPUID subleaf as four 32 bit groups carrying shift count, processor count, level number, level type, and APIC identity, with remaining bits reserved. Widths distinguish shift, count, level, type, and identity fields.

Legacy core counting views a CPUID register as cache type plus a core count field with an intervening unused span, where zero type means absent and the architectural count is one more than the encoded value.
ABI fact: supported topology leaves are 0x0b and 0x1f sharing one domain mapping and limit, plus 0x80000026 with its own mapping and limit; any other leaf value is unsupported.
ABI fact: legacy core discovery requires CPUID level at least 4 with nonzero cache type in leaf 4 subleaf 0, while synthetic topology is reported when CPUID level is below 1.
ABI fact: AMD node relative core adjustment applies below family 0x17 when more than one node per package exists; ancient legacy handling applies only to family 5.

ABI fact: bank 4 is treated as implicitly able to raise threshold interrupts while other banks depend on a present indication in the high status half; hardware identity and type combine with hardware identity in the high half word.

Enumeration rejects a subleaf with zero processor count or invalid type, reports and assigns a successor domain index for out of range types without advancing the last domain tracker, and otherwise translates through the leaf mapping and advances the tracker, then records APIC identity on the root domain and warns once on later mismatch before programming shift and count.

Legacy parsing derives core shift from legacy core count order, and when hyperthreading is present derives thread shift from the leaf 1 processor count shift minus core shift under a one time warning guard, then folds thread bits into core shift and scales core count before programming thread and core domains.

Identifier assignment derives package and die identifiers by shifting the APIC value, derives logical package die and core identifiers only outside early boot, derives package relative core identifier by masking to package scope and shifting past thread bits, copies AMD node identity, and invokes AMD fixup only for AMD vendor.
Shift helper returns the identifier unchanged for the thread domain and otherwise shifts right by the preceding domain shift; mask helper yields a low bit mask of width equal to the domain shift.
Synthetic topology programs both thread and core domains with zero shift and single count, and signals synthetic mode exactly when CPUID level is below 1.
AMD fixup leaves core identity unchanged except on older families with multiple nodes per package, where it reduces core identity modulo per node core count.

Generic discovery clears extended level, handles absence of CPUID with a non CPUID path and early return, otherwise performs scan, detection, vendor resolution, Intel leaf unlocking, capability and address size capture, default naming, and on 32 bit builds marks a known return defect.

Capability merging treats the boot processor record as accumulator: secondary processors narrow shared feature words by intersection and broaden bug words by union, after forced capability overrides have been applied around vendor and generic adjustments.

Machine check capability capture masks bank count from the global capability register, clamps excess to a build maximum with a warning, stores the per CPU count, and preinitializes each bank control to all ones with init marked true before vendor quirks and final programming.

Generic setup enables global control only when hardware reports control present, while bank preparation optionally logs retained errors from prior reset without dispatching them and then for each enabled bank writes control, clears status, and rereads control to confirm continued enablement.

Ancient handling accepts only family 5 and dispatches Intel and Centaur to legacy initializers while recording a mode flag and reporting handled; all other vendors and families report unhandled. Modern vendor setup dispatches Intel, AMD with Hygon, Centaur, and Zhaoxin to dedicated initializers and ignores others.
Fallback legacy initializers in the internal header are defined as empty operations, so builds using them perform no machine check actions for those paths.

AMD feature setup walks every per CPU bank and up to a fixed block count, using scalable addressing when enabled and legacy addressing otherwise, aborting a bank on missing address or failed safe read, skipping entries without valid indication or without usable threshold support or with locked state, and otherwise preparing threshold state.

Scalable MCA configuration acknowledges extended register use, conditionally enables deferred interrupt type for APIC delivery when supported unset and desired, conditionally enables corrected threshold interrupt when present and desired, records status and address validity hints, then reads identity and matches combined hardware and type codes against a table to assign type handle identity and per type instance number.

Block address resolution first bounds checks bank and block, then for scalable mode uses direct per bank and per block registers gated by a pointer mask, and for legacy mode uses control register mapping for block zero, pointer derived extended address for block one, and sequential advance thereafter.

Threshold limit selection prefers a firmware supplied value when nonzero and otherwise falls back to a build maximum, clamped to that maximum; one build provides a constant zero accessor while the threshold build returns a stored global, and block init applies the chosen limit with restart state carrying LVT offset.

Threshold APIC vector installation occurs only when no reservation is held and vector installation succeeds, in which case the new offset becomes the reservation; otherwise the prior reservation is preserved. Threshold block setup records interrupt capability and enables interrupts only when capable, tracking threshold banks accordingly.

CPU bringup progresses from defaults through generic discovery, topology parsing, vendor identification, forced overrides, default fencing, vendor initialization, bus handling, serial handling, memory protection setup, feature filtering and dependency validation, model naming, random and key and control flow setup, second forced override, symmetric merge, health init, to NUMA attachment, with no return to earlier phases.

Machine check bringup progresses from disabled and ancient checks through availability, capability capture, pool allocation with disable on failure, initialized marking, timer arming, generic enable, vendor customization, bank programming, to control register enablement; legacy family 5 exits early after its dedicated path.

AMD threshold bringup progresses per bank from quirk and vector setup to scalable configuration or legacy threshold disable, then per block from address resolution to safe read to validity and capability filtering to threshold preparation, with bank abort on addressing or read failure and block skip on invalid or unusable entries.

Firmware may report inconsistent APIC identities across subleaves or undefined domain types; the code warns once and either preserves the first identity or assigns a successor domain without updating the tracker, so later topology math may rest on synthetic ordering.

Legacy thread shift subtracts core order from a firmware supplied processor shift; an undersized firmware value triggers a one time warning and leaves thread shift at zero, collapsing thread and core levels rather than failing.
Logical identifier lookup can fail for out of range or unpopulated levels, and callers must handle negative errors; mask computation assumes shift widths that keep a 32 bit shift defined.

Hardware may report more banks than supported, allocation of the record pool may fail, and status registers may retain prior reset errors; the code clamps with warning, disables further handling on allocation failure, and logs retained errors without dispatch until late consumers register.

Scalable MCA register reads may fail; configuration tolerates control read failure, warns and aborts identity matching on identity read failure, and threshold enumeration aborts a bank on address absence or safe read failure rather than using stale values.
